-Search rule for tasks whose exact target is not initially visible: run a single forward sweep that does not oscillate. Treat each inspected receptacle as consumed; the next move should go to a different receptacle, ideally one not just inspected. Use the numbered receptacle names as a local progress cue: after checking an instance of a family, prefer the next higher-numbered unvisited instance or a wholly uninspected family or surface instead of jumping back to an earlier location. Open each closed container once and read its contents; if it is empty, continue forward to a new receptacle rather than cycling back through earlier ones. +Search rule for tasks whose exact target is not initially visible: run a single outward sweep that does not oscillate. Treat the receptacle you have just inspected as consumed for this search: the next move should go to a different receptacle, preferably a higher-numbered instance of the same family that you have not just inspected, or a family or surface you have not yet reached in this sweep, instead of jumping back to a lower-numbered or just-visited location. Use the visible numbered receptacle names as this local progress cue; do not rely on a global visited set. Open each closed container once upon reaching it and read its contents; if it lacks the target, continue forward to a new receptacle rather than cycling back through earlier ones. Check easily reached surfaces (countertops, desks, beds, tables, shelves) early, before exhausting one closed-container family. Continue until the exact requested category is found or all plausible receptacles have been inspected once, keeping within the step budget. This consumed-receptacle rule governs only the search for the initially hidden first target; it does not forbid returning to a known source that visibly still holds another exact instance when the task requires several instances.

The current Parent has no temperature step, so this is a new proposal rather than a re-imposed rule that already failed; the fallback for an unavailable action and the no-cycle clause leave no adverse response to address.

Both current multi-instance runs already deliver the exact count sequentially by returning to the visible source for the second unit (`G3`, `P6:18`, `P6:24`, `P7:5`, `P7:10`), and `M9` records the same reachable-source behavior (e.g. `S1_R04/P8:8`, `S1_R04/P9:8`). The rule preserves that capability and its exclusion of the desklamp 'finish with one co-located target' constraint prevents that scoped rule from ending ordinary multi-instance tasks early, which is needed coordination rather than duplication; no adverse response is observed.
